thread:
anya: quick sync — i'm going to roll out the new client-side gating via headers next week. need to lock the canary scope, fallback rules, and who owns the runtime checks.

mike: +1. what header name are we standardizing on?

anya: thinking `x-rw-gate` for flag name + `x-rw-client` for client id/version. example: `x-rw-gate: new-text-composer=true` and `x-rw-client: sdk/1.6.0`

cheng: that sounds good. will the SDK include an automatic version check or do we expect server-side parsing?

anya: SDK will send the `x-rw-client` header. routing/edge will parse and decide canary eligibility. SDK should still expose an opt-in toggle so apps can override locally.

sam: for safety, prefer server defaults = opt-out for any breaking feature. non-breaking perf toggles can be opt-in by default.

mike: agree. important: behavior if header missing — treat as legacy client (opt-out). we can't silently change old clients.

anya: exactly. fallback rules: header missing => no gating; header present + version >= 1.5.0 => eligible per rollout policy; header present + version < 1.5.0 => explicit deny.

cheng: i'll add unit + e2e tests to the SDK to ensure `x-rw-client` value is emitted and formatted. canary-bot will validate presence on staging.

rollout-bot: FYI — policy draft: 5% traffic for first 48h (versions >= 1.5.0), escalate to 25% after automated health checks pass, then 100% a week later. health checks = error rate, latency p95, and quality regression alerts.

mike: who owns the health check thresholds? i.e., when does automation auto-roll back vs alert humans?

anya: ops + eng-runtime set thresholds. proposal: error rate +50% relative or +0.5% absolute (whichever smaller) triggers rollback; p95 +100ms triggers alert; eval quality regression triggers immediate rollback.

sam: we should also instrument sample responses to S3 for manual QA checks during canary. add a flag `collect-samples=true` controlled by rollout config.

cheng: noted. will add an optional `x-rw-sample: true` header on canary requests for sampling, and SDK will expose an opt-in telemetry hook.

mike: quick QA logistics — can we gate by user segments? e.g., internal@redwood.com and 5% of prod?

anya: yes, canary config supports audience rules: email domain allowlist, percentage rollouts, and SDK-version constraint. we'll include internal allowlist for immediate testing.

rollout-bot: config snippet saved to /configs/feature-rollouts/new-text-composer.yml (internal link) — will post PR when draft finalized.

mike: i'm putting up PR now for runtime checks and header parsing — https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/2897 : please review.

cheng: pinged on the PR. i'll review tests and add the sampling header case.

anya: owner: anya (rollout plan), cheng (sdk tests), mike (runtime parsing), sam (QA checklist).

sam: QA checklist items: smoke in staging, sample dump validation, perf baseline run, canary runbook steps + rollback playbook. i'll draft doc.

mike: small ask — add a compatibility shim in the client so older SDKs include a minimal `x-rw-client: sdk/legacy` header. reduces ambiguity.

anya: good idea. cheng can include that in the SDK patch.

cheng: will add `sdk/legacy` for <1.5.0 and explicit semver for newer releases.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: staging runtime patch deploy @ 2026-04-02T03:00Z.

anya: timeline: merge runtime PR by EOD Thu, SDK patch by Fri, staging tests Fri afternoon, start 5% canary Mon morning.

mike: tagging reviewers: @cheng @sam — i left comments in the PR about edge-cases (multiple flags in header, malformed values).

cheng: noted — i'll handle parsing robustness and add logging for malformed headers (rate limited).

sam: one more — analytics needs final event names for canary metrics so dashboards pick them up. @data-team please share naming conventions.

anya: i'll loop in data-team in the rollout doc. any objections to the plan? :eyes:

mike: none from me. :thumbsup:

cheng: looks good.

sam: going to write the runbook now and share a short checklist thread.

anya: thanks everyone — i'll post the final rollout doc and assign follow-ups.
